punchline: The famous 21 grams came from one patient out of six.
thirty_sec: In 1907 Dr Duncan MacDougall weighed six dying patients on a bed scale; one lost 21.3 grams at death, and the other five cases were flawed or inconsistent. A critic blamed sweat, and the experiment was never repeated.
question: Which success do you quote most, and how many comparable attempts sit behind it?
key_contrast: One clean result against five unclear ones.
